newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Ashanti happy with market forecast.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ashanti happy with market forecast.

text.p: Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd on Tuesday said market forecasts for its full 1997 and 1998 earnings were in line with its own expectations.
Analysts' estimates for 1997 earnings vary between $40 and $50 million. Commenting on this range, chief financial officer Mark Keatley said: "It's broadly correct."
Keatley said Ashanti had hedged 80 percent of next year's production at $428 per ounce of gold.
"We are quite well protected against the gold price and I think the analysts are therefore expecting a slight (earnings) increase next year which again is broadly correct," he told Reuters.
"Twenty percent of our production is still exposed to the gold price. So one cannot predict that, but we would expect there would be some increase (in 1998 earnings)," Keatly said.
Ashanti earlier reported 1997 second-quarter earnings fell to $7.7 million after a $2.5 million charge for redundancy costs, which compares with earnings of $13.4 million a year ago.
Ashanti reduced the workforce at its main Obuasi mine by 800 to just below 10,000.
The mine's production is set to increase in the second half of the year after just failing to meet first-half targets, Keatly said.
Obuasi produced 417,000 ounces in the first six months of the year against an objective of 420,000. Output was restricted by power supply disruptions and extraordinary rainfall, Keatly said.
But the gradual build-up of underground production and extraction of gold from an old part of the mine will boost overall output in the second half, he said.

Full 1998 profits will be underpinned by further cost reduction at Obuasi and the start-up in the second half of the year of the new Bibiani and Siguiri mines in respectively Ghana and Guinea, Keatly said.
